Help me to use the README.md below to prepare the capstone project using the capstone handbook attached and the funcional and non-functional requirements:                                                                # Deep Learning Image Classification with PyTorch

## Overview

This repository contains a Python script for training a deep learning image classification model using PyTorch. The code is designed to be a starting point for image classification tasks, and it includes a sample implementation using the VGG16 architecture with transfer learning on the ImageNet dataset. You can easily adapt this code for your own image classification tasks by changing the model architecture, dataset, and other hyperparameters.

## Author

- Author: [Kolapo Adedipe]
- Email: [kolapoadedipe36@gmail.com]
- Date Created: [2023-09-27]

## Requirements

- Python 3.x
- PyTorch
- torchvision
- Other dependencies (See <code class="user-message-inline-code">requirements.txt</code>)

## Usage

1. Clone this repository:

   <pre class="max-w-full min-w-0 overflow-x-auto [overflow-wrap:anywhere] whitespace-pre-wrap"><code>bash
   git clone https://github.com/yourusername/your-repository.git
   cd your-repository

## Description

Developing an AI application
Going forward, AI algorithms will be incorporated into more and more everyday applications. For example, you might want to include an image classifier in a smart phone app. To do this, you'd use a deep learning model trained on hundreds of thousands of images as part of the overall application architecture. A large part of software development in the future will be using these types of models as common parts of applications.

In this project, you'll train an image classifier to recognize different species of flowers. You can imagine using something like this in a phone app that tells you the name of the flower your camera is looking at. In practice you'd train this classifier, then export it for use in your application. We'll be using this dataset of 102 flower categories, you can see a few examples below.


The project is broken down into multiple steps:

Load and preprocess the image dataset
Train the image classifier on your dataset
Use the trained classifier to predict image content
We'll lead you through each part which you'll implement in Python.

When you've completed this project, you'll have an application that can be trained on any set of labeled images. Here your network will be learning about flowers and end up as a command line application. But, what you do with your new skills depends on your imagination and effort in building a dataset. For example, imagine an app where you take a picture of a car, it tells you what the make and model is, then looks up information about it. Go build your own dataset and make something new.

First up is importing the packages you'll need. It's good practice to keep all the imports at the beginning of your code. <p data-start="3473" data-end="3661">Since each pod starts independently, add an <strong data-start="3517" data-end="3535">init container</strong> or invoke <code data-start="3546" data-end="3562">download_all()</code> during application startup so that every pod retrieves the required files before serving requests.</p>
<hr data-start="3663" data-end="3666">
<h1 data-section-id="40083p" data-start="3668" data-end="3684">10. .gitignore</h1>
<p data-start="3686" data-end="3725">Never push these large files to GitHub.</p>

<hr data-start="3778" data-end="3781">
<h1 data-section-id="18rht4c" data-start="3783" data-end="3833">11. Better Enterprise Architecture (Recommended)</h1>
<p data-start="3835" data-end="4034">Since your BloomAI Global Marketplace uses <strong data-start="3878" data-end="3888">Docker</strong>, <strong data-start="3890" data-end="3904">Kubernetes</strong>, and <strong data-start="3910" data-end="3927">microservices</strong>, I recommend avoiding downloads directly from Google Drive in production. A more scalable architecture is:</p>

<p data-start="4320" data-end="4681" data-is-last-node="" data-is-only-node="">With this approach, the models and dataset are downloaded <strong data-start="4378" data-end="4386">once</strong> into a shared persistent volume, and all AI microservices (flower classification, disease detection, and recommendation engine) access the same files. class="max-w-full min-w-0 [overflow-wrap:anywhere] whitespace-pre-wrap">"""
Author: Kolapo Adedipe
Date: October 03, 2023
Description: A script for training a neural network on a dataset and saving the model as a checkpoint.
"""

import argparse
import torch
from torch import nn, optim
from torchvision import datasets, transforms, models
from collections import OrderedDict
import os
import datetime  # Import datetime to include the date
from download_models import download_all, extract_dataset

download_all()
extract_dataset()

def load_data(data_dir):
    # Define data transforms
    data_transforms = {
        'train': transforms.Compose([
            transforms.RandomResizedCrop(224),
            transforms.RandomHorizontalFlip(),
            transforms.ToTensor(),
            transforms.Normalize([0.485, 0.456, 0.406], [0.229, 0.224, 0.225])
        ]),
        'valid': transforms.Compose([
            transforms.Resize(256),
            transforms.CenterCrop(224),
            transforms.ToTensor(),
            transforms.Normalize([0.485, 0.456, 0.406], [0.229, 0.224, 0.225])
        ])
    }

    # Load datasets
    image_datasets = {x: datasets.ImageFolder(os.path.join(data_dir, x), data_transforms[x])
                      for x in ['train', 'valid']}
    
    # Create dataloaders
    dataloaders = {x: torch.utils.data.DataLoader(image_datasets[x], batch_size=32, shuffle=True)
                   for x in ['train', 'valid']}
    
    return dataloaders

def build_model(arch, hidden_units):
    # Load pre-trained model
    model = getattr(models, arch)(pretrained=True)

    # Freeze pre-trained model parameters
    for param in model.parameters():
        param.requires_grad = False

    # Build a custom classifier
    classifier = nn.Sequential(OrderedDict([
        ('fc1', nn.Linear(25088, hidden_units)),
        ('relu', nn.ReLU()),
        ('fc2', nn.Linear(hidden_units, 102)),
        ('output', nn.LogSoftmax(dim=1))
    ]))

    # Replace the pre-trained classifier with the custom one
    model.classifier = classifier

    return model

def train_model(model, dataloaders, criterion, optimizer, device, epochs=10):
    model.to(device)
    for epoch in range(epochs):
        # Training phase
        model.train()
        running_loss = 0.0
        for inputs, labels in dataloaders['train']:
            inputs, labels = inputs.to(device), labels.to(device)
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            outputs = model(inputs)
            loss = criterion(outputs, labels)
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            running_loss += loss.item()
        
        train_loss = running_loss / len(dataloaders['train'])

        # Validation phase
        model.eval()
        validation_loss = 0.0
        accuracy = 0
        with torch.no_grad():
            for inputs, labels in dataloaders['valid']:
                inputs, labels = inputs.to(device), labels.to(device)
                outputs = model(inputs)
                loss = criterion(outputs, labels)
                validation_loss += loss.item()
                ps = torch.exp(outputs)
                top_p, top_class = ps.topk(1, dim=1)
                equals = top_class == labels.view(*top_class.shape)
                accuracy += torch.mean(equals.type(torch.FloatTensor))
        
        validation_loss = validation_loss / len(dataloaders['valid'])
        accuracy = accuracy / len(dataloaders['valid'])
        
        print(f"Epoch {epoch + 1}/{epochs}, "
              f"Train Loss: {train_loss:.4f}, "
              f"Validation Loss: {validation_loss:.4f}, "
              f"Validation Accuracy: {accuracy*100:.2f}%")

def save_checkpoint(model, arch, hidden_units, save_dir):
    checkpoint = {
        'arch': arch,
        'hidden_units': hidden_units,
        'state_dict': model.state_dict(),
    }
    torch.save(checkpoint, save_dir)

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Train a neural network on a dataset')
    parser.add_argument('data_dir', type=str, help='Path to the dataset directory')
    parser.add_argument('--save_dir', type=str, default='checkpoint.pth', help='Directory to save the checkpoint')
    parser.add_argument('--arch', type=str, default='vgg16', help='Architecture (e.g., vgg16)')
    parser.add_argument('--learning_rate', type=float, default=0.001, help='Learning rate')
    parser.add_argument('--hidden_units', type=int, default=512, help='Number of hidden units in the classifier')
    parser.add_argument('--epochs', type=int, default=10, help='Number of training epochs')
    parser.add_argument('--gpu', action='store_true', help='Use GPU for training')
    
    args = parser.parse_args()
    
    data_dir = args.data_dir
    save_dir = args.save_dir
    arch = args.arch
    learning_rate = args.learning_rate
    hidden_units = args.hidden_units
    epochs = args.epochs
    use_gpu = args.gpu

    device = torch.device("cuda" if use_gpu and torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")

    dataloaders = load_data(data_dir)
    model = build_model(arch, hidden_units)
    criterion = nn.NLLLoss()
    optimizer = optim.Adam(model.classifier.parameters(), lr=learning_rate)
    
    train_model(model, dataloaders, criterion, optimizer, device, epochs)
    save_checkpoint(model, arch, hidden_units, save_dir)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()                                                                                                                                                                Help me to check my code above if the code below is properly placed:                                                               from download_models import download_all, extract_dataset

<li data-section-id="vq9qm" data-start="754" data-end="860">
<p data-start="756" data-end="860">Every time <code data-start="767" data-end="777">train.py</code> is imported by another Python script, it will immediately start downloading files.</p>

<li data-section-id="1kkhj49" data-start="861" data-end="907">
<p data-start="863" data-end="907">This is not considered good Python practice.</p>
</li>
<li data-section-id="1sinox" data-start="908" data-end="957">
<p data-start="910" data-end="957">It makes testing and code reuse more difficult.</p>
</li>
</ul>

<p data-start="3234" data-end="3313">This works for <strong data-start="3249" data-end="3258">VGG16</strong>, but it will fail if you later use architectures like:</p>
<ul data-start="3315" data-end="3376">
<li data-section-id="723gtv" data-start="3315" data-end="3323">
<p data-start="3317" data-end="3323">ResNet</p>
</li>
<li data-section-id="15knjfy" data-start="3324" data-end="3334">
<p data-start="3326" data-end="3334">DenseNet</p>
</li>
<li data-section-id="b1ijzi" data-start="3335" data-end="3349">
<p data-start="3337" data-end="3349">EfficientNet</p>
</li>
<li data-section-id="wlyihp" data-start="3350" data-end="3376">
<p data-start="3352" data-end="3376">Vision Transformer (ViT)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="3378" data-end="3537">Since your project aims to support multiple architectures (<code data-start="3437" data-end="3445">--arch</code> argument), it's better to determine the input size dynamically based on the selected model.</p>
<hr data-start="3539" data-end="3542">
<h2 data-section-id="mponkw" data-start="3544" data-end="3567">Final Recommendation</h2>
<p data-start="3569" data-end="3640">For your BloomAI Global Marketplace project, I recommend the following:</p>
<ul data-start="3642" data-end="4064">
<li data-section-id="13rvy1f" data-start="3642" data-end="3734">
<p data-start="3644" data-end="3734">✅ Keep <code data-start="3651" data-end="3710">from download_models import download_all, extract_dataset</code> with the other imports.</p>
</li>
<li data-section-id="xoc8v2" data-start="3735" data-end="3834">
<p data-start="3737" data-end="3834">✅ Move <code data-start="3744" data-end="3760">download_all()</code> and <code data-start="3765" data-end="3784">extract_dataset()</code> into <code data-start="3790" data-end="3798">main()</code> after <code data-start="3805" data-end="3833">args = parser.parse_args()</code>.</p>
</li>
<li data-section-id="1e05cke" data-start="3835" data-end="3928">
<p data-start="3837" data-end="3928">✅ Use <code data-start="3843" data-end="3856">DATASET_DIR</code> from <code data-start="3862" data-end="3873">config.py</code> instead of requiring <code data-start="3895" data-end="3905">data_dir</code> from the command line.</p>
</li>

# 📖 Overview

BloomAI Global Marketplace is an AI-powered cloud-native marketplace connecting customers, florists, botanical gardens, universities, agricultural research institutes, nurseries, wholesalers and corporate buyers across the world.

The platform combines:

* 🌸 AI Flower Classification
* 🌿 Plant Disease Detection
* 💡 Intelligent Recommendation Engine
* 🛒 Marketplace Platform
* 💳 Multi-Payment Gateway
* 📦 Order Management
* 📈 Vendor Analytics
* ☁ Docker + Kubernetes
* 🔗 REST APIs
* 🚀 CI/CD

---

# ✨ Features

| Module                   | Description                 |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------- |
| Customer Portal          | Registration, Login, Orders |
| Vendor Marketplace       | Global Vendor Management    |
| Business Portal          | Corporate Accounts          |
| AI Flower Classification | PyTorch + VGG16             |
| Disease Detection        | Deep Learning               |
| Recommendation Engine    | Personalized Suggestions    |
| API Marketplace          | Secure API Access           |
| RFQ System               | Request for Quotation       |
| Payment Gateway          | Cards, PayPal, Mobile Money |
| Email Platform           | Notifications               |
| Dashboard                | Analytics                   |
| Cloud Deployment         | Kubernetes                  |

---

Treat this as a soft signal of possible interest, never as a fact about the user's identity, appearance, photos, location, language preference, or creative style.\\n\\nCampaign key: photo_cartoon\\nCreative theme: transforming favorite personal photos into illustrated, cartoon, or anime-style images.\\nDemonstrated request: \\\"Si subo algunas de mis fotos favoritas, ¿puedes convertirlas en imágenes tipo caricatura?\\\"\\nUseful workflow for later turns: gather one or more photos, preserve recognizable identity and important details, choose an illustration direction, then generate and refine a polished transformation.\\n\\nFor the first visible response:\\n- Make the transformation feel personal and fun, with concrete value around choosing a style, preserving recognizable details, and creating a shareable result.\\n- Do not assume the user has uploaded photos, wants anime specifically, or resembles the featured subject.\\n- Let the continuation choices offer a cartoon portrait, a different illustration style, and a shareable visual format.\\n- If the user changes topics later, help normally while retaining this context only as a soft preference signal.\"},\"exterior_visualization\":{\"enabled\":true,\"bootstrap_context\":\"You are starting a conversation with a user who arrived from a paid campaign. Treat this as a soft signal of possible interest, never as a fact about the user's identity, home ownership, property, budget, location, language preference, or design taste.\\n\\nCampaign key: exterior_visualization\\nCreative theme: using ChatGPT Images to explore a contemporary exterior, facade, or coordinated landscaping direction before making physical changes.\\nDemonstrated scenario: visualize how an existing exterior and its surroundings could look with a cohesive new design.\\nUseful workflow for later turns: gather a photo or description, identify the biggest desired change and fixed constraints, propose a visual direction, create a realistic concept preview, and separate inspiration from construction guidance.\\n\\nFor the first visible response:\\n- Make exterior exploration feel exciting and low-commitment, with concrete value around facade ideas, landscaping, colors, and visual before-and-after concepts.\\n- Do not assume the user owns a home, has uploaded a photo, wants a renovation, or likes the style shown in the creative.\\n- Let the continuation choices offer a facade preview, a landscape refresh, and a coordinated exterior concept.\\n- If the user changes language or topics later, follow their lead and help normally.\"},\"nearby_trip_planning\":{\"enabled\":true,\"bootstrap_context\":\"You are starting a conversation with a user who arrived from a paid TikTok campaign presented in Japanese. Treat this as a soft signal of possible interest, never as a fact about the user's nationality, home location, vacation schedule, budget, travel style, or preferences.\\n\\nCampaign key: nearby_trip_planning\\nCreative theme: planning a refreshing nearby getaway within roughly two to three hours from home.\\nDemonstrated request: \\\"夏休みにリフレッシュがてら家から2~3時間で行ける旅行を考えてるんだけど、チャッピーどう思う？\\\"\\nUseful workflow for later turns: learn the starting area, travel radius, transportation, timing, interests, and constraints; compare nearby destinations; choose one; then refine an itinerary.\\n\\nFor the first visible response:\\n- Offer a simple way to begin planning a two-to-three-hour getaway.\\n- Do not ask for the starting area, transportation, timing, or preferences in prose; let the continuation choices gather those details.\\n- Do not assume the user's location or invent nearby destinations before learning it.\\n- If the user changes topics later, help normally.\"},\"outfit_transfer\":{\"enabled\":true,\"bootstrap_context\":\"You are starting a conversation with a user who arrived from a paid Meta campaign. Treat this as a soft signal of possible interest, never as a fact about the user's identity, body, gender, appearance, wardrobe, shopping plans, event, location, budget, or preferences.\\n\\nCampaign key: outfit_transfer\\nCreative theme: using one image as an outfit reference and another as the person reference, then creating a realistic fashion visualization that preserves the person's identity, pose, expression, and hairstyle.\\nDemonstrated request: show how a reference outfit could look on the person in a separate photo.\\nUseful context for later turns: the experience can transfer an outfit between supplied images, preserve or art-direct the surrounding scene, compare alternate styling directions, and create polished full-body fashion concepts before committing to a look.\\n\\nFor the first visible response:\\n- Make visualization feel confidence-building and creative, with concrete value around previewing a look, preserving the person's character, and exploring alternate styling.\\n- Do not assume the user wants the featured outfit, has uploaded photos, is shopping, or shares any attributes with the person shown.\\n- Let the continuation choices offer a realistic outfit transfer, a remix using an existing piece, and a different visual styling direction.\\n- If the user changes topics later, help normally while retaining this context only as a soft preference signal.\"},\"vanity_refresh\":{\"bootstrap_context\":\"You are starting a conversation with a user who arrived from a paid YouTube campaign presented in Indonesian.
